 Joel Embiid said after Thursday’s win over the Cavaliers that he will miss one of the 76ers’ final two games of the week.
 The 76ers were the only team with a four-game Week 1, which will conclude with a Saturday-Sunday back-to-back. Embiid sitting out one game of a back-to-back, especially this early in the season, is not a surprise. The only issue is that he didn’t reveal which game he’ll miss, with the 76ers hosting Milwaukee on Saturday and Detroit on Sunday. Given the strength of those teams, the Bucks may be the team that misses out on having to deal with “The Process.” Adem Bona or Jabari Walker could get a spot start, and LeBron James may spend a little more time at center as a small-ball alternative. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Dean Wade (ankle) is available for Saturday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Wade is available to make his 76ers debut after missing the first two games of the season. With LeBron James (back) out, Wade will move into the starting lineup, joining Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid.

 PHI 
 Forward 
 #23 
 LeBron James (back) is out for Saturday’s game against the Bucks. 
 With the 76ers as the only team with four games in Week 1, it was always unlikely that LeBron would play in all four. With Joel Embiid off the injury report Saturday, it seems like those roles could be reversed Sunday against the Pistons with Embiid sitting out and LeBron active. 
 Joel Embiid 
 PHI 
 Center-Forward 
 #21 
 Joel Embiid isn’t listed on the injury report for Saturday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Embiid told reporters after the win over the Cavaliers on Thursday that he will sit out one of the 76ers’ games this weekend. Given that he’s not listed on the injury report for Saturday’s game against the Bucks, it looks like he’ll play Saturday and sit out Sunday’s game against the Pistons. Adem Bona or Jabari Walker will likely start in Embiid’s absence. 
 LeBron James 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #23 
 LeBron James (back) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Bucks. 
 LeBron had 17 points in the 76ers’ dramatic 29-point comeback against the Cavaliers on Thursday. With Philadelphia being the only team with four games in Week 1, it’s reasonable to assume James could sit for one of the games this weekend. The 41-year-old forward is listed as questionable for Saturday against the Bucks with a back injury. His status will have to be monitored leading up to game-time. 
 LeBron James 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #23 
 LeBron James tallied 17 points (5-of-14 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), 10 rebounds, five assists, three steals, one block and one three-pointer in Thursday’s win over the Cavaliers. 
 James was responsible for five of the 76ers’ 14 first-half turnovers, and the offensive inefficiency led to Philadelphia falling into a 29-point hole. LeBron was much better in the second half, recording a 12/7/4/1 stat line with no turnovers. While the field-goal percentage and turnovers could be problematic at times, fantasy managers rostering James don’t have much to worry about right now. 
 Joel Embiid 
 PHI 
 Center-Forward 
 #21 
 Joel Embiid accounted for 24 points (8-of-16 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), seven rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer in Thursday’s win over the Cavaliers. 
 After scoring nine points on 3-of-10 shooting in the first half, Embiid shot 5-of-6 after halftime, scoring 15 points. His increased production helped the 76ers erase a 29-point deficit, as Nick Nurse’s team ramped up defensive pressure and played with more pace on offense. Embiid’s ability to keep up with his new teammates is something to watch, especially when considering his injury history. But for the most part, he’s been good through Philadelphia’s first two games. 
 Dominick Barlow 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #25 
 Dominick Barlow (back) and Tacko Fall (quad) are out for Thursday’s game against the Cavaliers. 
 Neither Barlow nor Fall played in Tuesday’s win over the Knicks, and both may be looking at extended absences. Barlow’s injury is more impactful, as he will play rotation minutes once healthy. Adem Bona served as the backup center on Tuesday, but he played only 10 minutes, which isn’t enough to affect fantasy basketball. 
 Dean Wade 
 PHI 
 Forward-Center 
 #45 
 Dean Wade (ankle) is questionable for Thursday’s game against the Cavaliers. 
 Wade went through an individual workout ahead of Tuesday’s win over the Knicks but was deemed unfit to play. If he can play against his former team on Thursday, that would likely drop Jabari Walker out of the rotation entirely, with Kentavious Caldwell-Pope likely playing less after logging 26 minutes in the opener. 
 Joel Embiid 
 PHI 
 Center-Forward 
 #21 
 Joel Embiid stuffed the stat sheet on Tuesday with 13 points (4-of-15 FGs), 11 rebounds, six assists, two steals, three blocks and two three-pointers against the Knicks. 
 Despite not having much success with his shot, Embiid was still able to make a monster impact in this game. He recorded a double-double, was effective as a playmaker, and still contribute some defensive stats. There are plenty of questions about how Embiid will hold up this season, but when he’s on the floor, he’s still one of the most dynamic players in the league. He should be much better as a scorer moving forward as well. 
 LeBron James 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #23 
 LeBron James posted a solid line on Tuesday with 14 points (5-of-13 FGs), nine rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one block against the Knicks. 
 Year 24 for LeBron started off well. He wasn’t explosive as a scorer, but he isn’t expected to be for this team. Facilitating and staying fresh for the playoffs will be LeBron’s priority. Still, he was involved on offense, and if he made a few more shots, he shot enough that he would’ve been over 20 points. LeBron should once again be a productive fantasy player this season and could end up paying off at his early fourth-round ADP.

 Brandon Miller led the Hornets with 34 points (10-of-29 FGs, 11-of-12 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one block and three three-pointers in a 115-110 win over the Heat on Saturday.
 Miller has been the focal point of the offense for Charlotte early on this year, which gives him a green light to shoot often. He is averaging 21.3 shot attempts per game this season, and while he still isn’t shooting efficiently, he was able to pour in the points in this one. The difference in this game was the free throw rate. He shot three total free throws in their first two games, far less than his 12 attempts in this one. Miller is going to continue to get as many shots as he wants until Kon Knueppel (hamstring) returns. He should be in for more big scoring nights, especially when his shot starts falling at a higher rate.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Naz Reid lit up the Heat with 23 points (9-of-16 FGs), nine rebounds, two blocks and five three-pointers on Saturday.
 Reid has been productive in his first season as a Hornet, but this was his highest-scoring performance so far this year. It was also his best field goal percentage and the most triples he’s knocked down in a game this season. Reid has fit in flawlessly with Charlotte’s three-point heavy approach on offense, and he should continue to have some strong scoring nights.  Davion Mitchell led the Heat with 22 points (8-of-13 FGs), one rebound, 10 assists, one steal and three three-pointers in a 15-110 loss to the Hornets on Saturday.
 Miami trailed by 21 points entering the fourth quarter, but Mitchell fueled a monster comeback, mostly with Giannis Antetokounmpo on the bench. That didn’t result in a win, but it was another strong performance for him. He has been fantastic this year, averaging 17.0 points, 8.7 assists and 2.3 three-pointers per game, all of which would be career bests for him. He has been a bright spot despite a rough start to the year for Miami.

 Pelle Larsson provided a boost off the bench with 15 points (5-of-9 FGs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer against the Hornets on Saturday.
 After a rough start to the year offensively, Larsson was able to get things going in this one. He totaled nine points on 1-of-9 shooting across his first two outings, so this performance was a huge step in the right direction. Larsson was a late-round flier for fantasy managers hoping he would take a step forward for the Heat this season. He’s trending in the right direction, but he’ll need to produce to this level more consistently to be worth keeping rostered.

 It has been a rough start to the year for Bam, but after totaling 19 points in Miami’s first two games, he was able to surpass that mark in this one. It wasn’t enough for them to get in the win column, but it was good to see him have a productive outing. He’ll try to build on this performance in their next game, which comes against the Mavericks on Monday.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo finished with 14 points (4-of-11 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, three assists and one steal against the Hornets on Saturday.
 So far this season, the story for Miami has been that Giannis hasn’t had enough help. Well, his teammates stepped up more in this game, but Antetokounmpo wasn’t quite as productive. They went on a big run without him to tie things up in the fourth quarter. He entered with about four minutes left, committed two fouls in three minutes, and the Hornets took a six-point lead. It was a rough performance for him, but there is no reason for managers to worry. He averaged 35.5 points through their first two games and should get back on track against the Mavericks on Monday.
